key_insight: A hard-trace first-order neural formulation can solve coupled Stokes-Brinkman-Darcy flow by enforcing interface and boundary physics exactly while avoiding second derivatives.
engineering_relevance: This gives a physics-consistent surrogate for free-flow/porous-flow coupling with better pressure accuracy and a path to more reliable multiphysics simulations in filtration and porous media design.
method: Mixed first-order variables: stress, Darcy flux, and pressure-gradient auxiliaries remove second derivatives from the network.
Hard constraints: shared interface traces, boundary liftings, and traction maps enforce kinematic and force-balance conditions exactly.
Pressure correction: an integral momentum relation recovers pressure after training without reference-pressure labels.
evidence_signal: Across two manufactured tests and three permeabilities, corrected upper-pressure relative L2 error was 0.87%–2.58%, and correction improved both upper-pressure L2 and Brinkman-pressure H1 errors in every run; a filtration case also matched a refined FEM reference.
watch_item: The approach relies on careful construction of hard constraints and post-training pressure correction, so implementation complexity and sensitivity to interface/boundary specification may be a practical concern.
paper_title: Hard-Trace First-Order Residual Learning for Coupled Stokes-Brinkman-Darcy Flow
